strengths: The fix restores the exact client-side filter that existed in the parent (filteredBySearch over name/email, rendered as rows), which is the correct option because the users backend has no search support — no UI control silently no-ops.

The regression test is genuinely non-vacuous: the mock deliberately ignores the `search` param and returns both rows, so the assertion that the non-matching row disappears can only pass if the client-side filter is applied; it is a real RED→GREEN guard rather than a tautology.

Sort state is kept out of loadUsers' dependency list via sortRef/cursorRef, so sort/page changes do not re-trigger the mount effect and reset the page; reset rules (sort/filter → cursor=0, paging → preserve) are applied explicitly at each call site.

sortableColumns is the exact rendered-keys ∩ allowlist intersection including both created_at and updated_at, with 'action' inert — no phantom sortable column that would silently fall back server-side.

Dummy parity is achieved through the shared compareRows/paginate/formatDateTime helpers rather than bespoke logic, covering created_at-DESC→id-DESC fallback, offset slice, total=filtered.length and summary, with zero network.
All three commits stayed strictly within the 3 in-scope files; assignUserRole is byte-identical and assignDummyUserRole is untouched, so the role PATCH flow is preserved.

issues.description: loadUsers is a useCallback keyed on [roleFilter, search] and the mount effect depends on loadUsers, so editing the search input or the role Select fires an immediate fetch (cursor=0) on each change in addition to the explicit 'Terapkan filter' click — a redundant request per keystroke. This is the established pattern inherited from the products/outlets pages and does not violate the spec's reset rule, so it is non-blocking.

page.test.tsx is 432 lines across five nested describe blocks. Test files are naturally long and this mirrors the already-approved products/outlets page.test.tsx, so it is not treated as a blocking split; noted only as a maintainability observation.
